title: Quant presets and calibration playbook for model catalog defaults
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create an operational playbook and implementation ticket set to choose, validate, and publish per-model quantization presets (FP8/INT8) in the model catalog with automated calibration runs and accuracy validation. The goal is to provide safe, documented defaults that ship with each catalog entry, plus automated guardrails and rollback behavior so customers get predictable quality/cost trade-offs without manual experimentation.
background: We currently have ad-hoc quant profiles and several exploratory kernels for INT8 and FP8. Teams and customers want catalog-level defaults so hosted and dedicated customers can rely on a known performance/accuracy envelope. Existing experiments are scattered across PRs and bench runs; we need a repeatable pipeline, a validation harness, and explicit guardrails for rollout.
proposal: Build a calibration + evaluation pipeline that: (1) runs a calibrated quantization sweep per model (FP8 variants and INT8 with and without per-channel), (2) collects accuracy regressions against a golden prompt set and downstream evals, (3) computes cost/latency estimates, (4) selects a default preset per model with metadata fields (preset id, expected perf delta, confidence score), and (5) publishes presets into the catalog with associated safety thresholds and automated rollback triggers.
calibration_playbook:
Step 1: Ingest model artifact and baseline FP32 performance profile.
Step 2: Generate representative calibration dataset for the model family (mix of short/long prompts, instruction vs. completion). Use seeded sampling + producer scripts in /infra/quant/seeded-samp.
Step 3: Run automated sweep: FP8-e4m3, FP8-e5m2, INT8-symmetric, INT8-asymmetric, INT8-per-channel. Each run produces: token-level divergence metrics, top-k ngram overlap, logprob KL, and downstream eval scores.
Step 4: Run latency and memory profiler on target hardware variants (A100, H100, T4-equivalent) using runtime kernels. Capture 50th/95th/99th latencies and max-resident memory.
Step 5: Compute per-preset utility score = weighted(accuracy_drop, cost_savings, latency_gain). Weights configurable per project.
Step 6: Apply guardrails: reject presets with >2% absolute drop on high-priority evals or >0.5 BLEU/ROUGE loss on translation/summarization families. Mark borderline presets as "beta" with customer opt-in.
Step 7: Emit catalog metadata (preset_id, baseline_delta_pct, expected_latency_change_ms, confidence_score, recommended_tier).
Step 8: Schedule staged rollout: internal canaries -> public beta -> default for non-enterprise tenants -> enterprise opt-in.
Step 9: Continuously monitor telemetry and trigger automated rollback if live drift in accuracy or latency exceeds thresholds for 3 consecutive samples.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline runs end-to-end on at least 5 models covering small/medium/large families and produces catalog metadata artifacts
Automated evaluator computes accuracy metrics and utility score with configurable weights
Catalog UI and API show a stable default preset field with expected perf deltas and a confidence score
Rollout orchestration exists for canary/beta/default with automated rollback conditions
Playbook documented in Confluence with step-by-step run commands and runbook for remediation
test_plan: Select test set: 3 instruction-following tasks, 2 summarization prompts, 2 code-generation prompts, 1 dialog scenario per model family
Run baseline FP32 and compare FP8/INT8 candidates using the calibration pipeline
Verify telemetry hooks: token divergence, latency histograms, top-k overlap metrics are emitted to the console backend
Simulate production traffic with loadgen for 24h on a canary pool and confirm no P95 increase >15%
Introduce synthetic data drift and verify rollback is triggered and documented in console audit logs
rollout_plan: phase-0: internal QA (sdc env) with feature flag, 1 week
phase-1: 5% external traffic beta with opt-in flag for customers, 2 weeks
phase-2: widen to 25% for non-SLA tenants, monitor 2 weeks
phase-3: set default for new catalog entries and non-SLA tenants if stable; enterprise customers remain opt-in unless they accept defaults
rollback: immediate revert on metric breach with automatic incident creation and postmortem template populated
metrics_and_alerts: accuracy_regression_pct per model family (alert if >1.5% over baseline for 3 samples)
eval_score_drop on sentinel prompt set (alert if >threshold configured per model)
latency_P95 increase (alert if >20% relative to baseline)
rollback_count and time-to-revert (SLO: revert within 5 minutes for automated rollbacks)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: calibration set not representative -> Mitigation: expand seeded sampling across customer telemetry buckets and include adversarial prompts
Risk: hardware-specific kernel bugs for FP8 on certain infra -> Mitigation: include hardware gating in pipeline and require cross-hardware validation
Risk: silent semantic degradation not captured by metrics -> Mitigation: add targeted human-in-the-loop checks for high-risk families and random audit sampling
Risk: customers relying on defaults unexpectedly see behavior changes -> Mitigation: make defaults opt-in for enterprise for first 3 months and provide clear changelog + migration guide
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Chose to support both FP8-e4m3 and INT8-per-channel as candidate families instead of committing to one. Rationale: FP8 shows strong latency gains on H100 but INT8 provides more predictable accuracy in some transformer variants.
2026-03-02: Set accuracy hard-guard at 2% absolute drop on primary evals for green preset. Borderline presets labeled as 'beta' and require opt-in.
2026-03-05: Decided not to auto-apply defaults to enterprise-managed Private deployments without explicit consent. Defaults will be metadata-only for Private until customer opt-in
implementation_notes: Calibration jobs will live under infra/quant-calib. Use the new quant-agent container image quant-agent:2026-03. We will reuse the eval harness from /bench/eval-harness but extend it to compute KL and top-k overlap. Add a lightweight manifest file (CSV) that lists golden prompt IDs, expected scores, and threshold columns. Telemetry tags: model_name, preset_id, run_id, hardware_target.
next_steps: 1) Land infra PRs to add quant-agent job types (ENG-24619). 2) Produce a seed calibration dataset for first 5 models (ENG-24620). 3) Wire telemetry and dashboard tiles (ENG-24621). Schedule weekly sync with PM/Design to review beta findings.
notes: Early runs show FP8-e4m3 reduces P95 by ~12% on H100 for 13B-class models with <1% delta on instruction evals. Larger 70B-class models see mixed accuracy; these will be flagged as beta. We must expand sentence-level semantic checks before expanding defaults to LLM-large family.
